issue_context.title: systemd-boot: Add option to change menu timeout in bootctl
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
It seems I accidentally increased the timeout in the boot menu to 301 seconds, I probably pressed `t` too much while booting or something similar. Now there is no (easy) way to remove this from a running system, working with `efivar` for a beginner is tricky since it's exporting hex code.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Show the timeout in `bootctl status` and make it possible to change it since systemd-boot already has access to efi vars. Something like
```
$ bootctl status
...
Current Boot Loader:
      Product: systemd-boot v246.6-3.fc33
      Boot menu timeout: 30 seconds
...

$ bootctl set-timeout 5
```

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
None

**The systemd version you checked that didn't have the feature you are asking for**
v246.6

review_comments: you are not ignroing the error here, you are failing (and rightly so), hence drop the ", ignoring". Also, I think it would be more useful to show the string that failed parsing instead of the error code (which most likely will be EINVAL anyway), i.e. replace %m by %s and include the argument as param
This initialization is not necessary… Maybe just fold it into one line `char16_t *encoded = utf8_to_utf16(…);`.
